rows.question: Which company's revised specification set the voltage that the Apollo 13 tank switches could not handle?

rows.answer:
North American Aviation is the company whose revised specification set the voltage. Its 1965 revision of the heater specification moved the tank heaters to 65 volts, and it was the prime contractor for the command and service module. The switches were built for a much lower voltage, so they were never updated to match. The switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC, and the heater specification was later raised to 65 volts without any change to the switches. The company revised the oxygen tank heater specification in 1965 to run at 65 volts, but the switches were not changed.

Beech Aircraft made the tanks under North American Aviation, and did not change the tank thermostatic switches when the heater specification moved to 65 volts. The company that revised the specification, though, was North American Aviation.
